originalTitle: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Tuesday
simplifiedContent: Here's what you need to know about the stock market right now: Indian stock markets didn't start the week strongly due to global concerns. However, good earnings reports from companies helped balance out the negative feelings about global tensions. Some analysts are looking at US job numbers, which were weaker than expected, and are now waiting to see what happens with inflation to figure out what will happen with interest rates. This mix of good and bad news is affecting how investors feel about the market. Overall, it's a bit of a uncertain time for the stock market right now.

originalTitle: Milky Mist Dairy Food mops up ₹465 crore from anchor investors ahead of IPO
simplifiedContent: Milky Mist Dairy Food, a company that is about to sell its shares to the public for the first time, has already raised ₹465.29 crore from big investors. This happened before the company's shares are open to everyone to buy, which will start on August 11. The company is selling its shares for ₹133-140 each, and the minimum amount you need to invest is ₹14,980. The share sale will close on August 13, and the company's shares are expected to start trading on the stock market on August 18. This is important because it shows that big investors are interested in the company, which could be a good sign for other investors.

originalTitle: NSE indices rejig: Vodafone Idea, Wipro part of major changes in Nifty Next 50 and Nifty 100. Check full list
simplifiedContent: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) is making some big changes to the groups of companies it tracks, called indices. This change will happen on September 30 and will affect lists like the Nifty 100 and Nifty Next 50. Some companies, including Vodafone Idea and Wipro, will be added to these lists, while others will be removed. This matters because it can affect how investors think about and invest in these companies. The changes will give a boost to the companies being added, as they may attract more investor attention and money.

originalTitle: This new-age tech stock hits over 4-year high, recovers 70% from March lows. Are you holding it?
simplifiedContent: The stock price of One97 Communications, the company that owns Paytm, has gone up by 10% to ₹1,598. This is a 4-year high for the company, meaning its stock hasn't been this valuable in over 4 years. The increase happened after a company called Bernstein said it thinks the stock could be worth even more, ₹2,200, because Paytm might make more money from fees related to a payment system called UPI. This is a big deal because the stock has recovered 70% from its low point in March, meaning it has gained back a lot of its value. This could be important for people who already own the stock, as its value is increasing.

originalTitle: Nippon India Equity buys stake in Iris Clothings that has risen 250% in five years
simplifiedContent: Nippon India Equity has invested in a company called Iris Clothings. The company's stock has done very well, going up by 250% over the past five years. This means that if you had invested in the company five years ago, your investment would be worth two and a half times more today. The stock has been consistently rising over the past year, reaching new highs and making money for its investors. This makes Iris Clothings one of the most successful investments in recent times, creating a lot of wealth for those who own its stock.

originalTitle: Wall Street slips ahead of inflation data, crude oil surges
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the stock market: the main stock indexes, like the S&P 500, Dow Jones, and Nasdaq, are experiencing small changes. The S&P 500 is barely up, while the Dow Jones and Nasdaq are slightly down. This means that the overall value of the stocks in these indexes is not changing much. The market is likely waiting to see what happens with upcoming inflation data, which could affect how stocks perform. The small changes in the indexes indicate a cautious mood among investors.
